item.title: #3592340: Show changes to the layout in the preview immediately, and keep stale server renders from undoing them
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 17 files, +985/−76 · js +983/−76 · md +2
  • Diff: 3061a42
  • Discussion: #3592340 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

In the Canvas editor, moving, deleting or dropping a component from the library now updates the preview straight away instead of after the server has rendered a new page. Dragged components no longer appear to jump back before landing. When several edits happen quickly, an older server render that arrives late no longer briefly removes the newer edit. A component moved by dragging is now also selected, as already happened for components added from the library.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

A new RTK listener middleware, optimisticPreviewListener (registered in makeStore), reacts to moveNode, shiftNode and deleteNode, so every trigger (drag and drop, context menu, "Move into", hotkeys) gets the same behaviour. It edits the DOM of the active preview iframe (getPreviewDocument()) using the canvas-start-…/canvas-end-… comment markers found via discoverCanvasBoundaries from @drupal-canvas/preview-geometry. optimisticPreview.ts provides movePreviewComponent, removePreviewComponent and insertPreviewComponent. Insertion uses the component's default_markup and css; the markup is parsed through a <template> so scripts do not run, and CSS goes in the head before the PREVIEW_HEAD_STYLES_ID style. Empty slot and region placeholders are hidden when a component lands in them, but a container that becomes empty after a move is not given a placeholder until the server render arrives. If markers are missing (for example a headless, cross-origin preview), the functions return false and the drag handler falls back to the earlier 'pending move' state.

To stop stale renders undoing these edits, previewEdits.ts keeps a module-level counter (notePreviewEdit, previewEditCount, isPreviewEditedSince). setHtml now takes the edit count at request time, stored as selectPreviewHtmlEditsAtRequest. IFrameSwapper skips applying HTML (in place or by swap) when the shown preview has been edited since that HTML was requested, and also checks this again when a loaded document is about to be swapped in. Prop edits made while typing in code component forms (createComponentFormStateHandler) also count as preview edits. Renders superseded by other changes, such as typing, still show. The server-rendered document still replaces the preview afterwards, correcting what the immediate edit approximates. useDropFromLayoutHandler now calls setSelectedComponent on the moved component.

item.title: #3592327: A code component cannot get the URL of a referenced entity, so a list of `content-entity-reference`s cannot (reliably) link to its items
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Critical feature request
  • Version: 1.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 7 files, +97/−18 · php +83/−12 · mdx +9/−1 · yml +5/−5
  • Diff: 9980955
  • Discussion: #3592327 · 1 contributor · 6 comments

Summary

Code components that receive a content-entity-reference prop (for example a list of related news items) can now link to each referenced entity. Every entity object handed to the component carries a __url key with the entity's canonical URL, so no field pick is needed. Previously the only option was the URL alias pick, which is empty for any entity without an alias, such as taxonomy terms on a fresh site.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and front-end developers.

  • Theme change: Code components that linked via the path␞␟alias pick should switch to __url.
  • New API: Every resolved content-entity-reference payload object now includes __url, the canonical URL of the entity or null.

Technical details

JsComponent::buildReferencePayload() now builds the payload as ['__type' => $entity->bundle(), '__url' => $url]. This applies to nested referenced entities too, since they go through the same method. The URL is generated only when !$entity->isNew() && $entity->hasLinkTemplate('canonical'), using toUrl('canonical')->toString(TRUE). The code does not call toUrl() without a relationship because EntityBase::toUrl() falls back to edit-form, which must not be exposed as a link to a referenced entity. Entity types with no canonical link template, such as file, get __url of null. The GeneratedUrl cacheability (for example path alias dependencies) is added to the payload's cacheability alongside the entity and negotiated language.

This is direction A from the issue's options table. The picker, expression syntax and entityFields are unchanged, and a __url is generated for every referenced entity whether or not the component uses it. The agent documentation now describes __type and __url. The test component canvas_test_code_components_news_list uses __url instead of the path␞␟alias pick.

Upgrade

Code components that linked to referenced entities through the alias pick can read __url instead and drop the pick from dataDependencies.entityFields:

const { label, __url: url } = featuredNews ?? {};
// ...
<a href={url}>{label}</a>

Remove 'ℹ︎␜entity:node:news_item␝path␞␟alias' from the prop's expressions.

item.title: #3592231: Workspaces PR 9: Stage a new page as published so one workspace publish makes it live
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Major unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 13 files, +341/−50 · php +310/−30 · js +19/−15 · md +12/−5
  • Diff: 6ffbba3
  • Discussion: #3592231 · 1 contributor · 5 comments

Summary

On the 1.x-workspaces branch, a page created in the Canvas editor while a workspace is active is now staged as published, so a single workspace publish makes it live. Before, it went live unpublished and the editor had to stage the status and publish a second time. A content template created in a workspace is now created disabled, so the core display keeps rendering for every visitor until the template's first draft is published with the workspace. Before, it was saved to Live enabled with an empty component tree and rendered that view mode empty.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

Config has no workspace storage and core keeps the Live default revision of a workspace-created entity unpublished, then promotes pending revisions verbatim. For pages, ApiContentControllers::post() now defaults status to the new private createsPublished(), which is TRUE when workspaceManager->hasActiveWorkspace(). Core's WorkspaceProviderBase::entityPresave() and entityInsert() then save an unpublished default revision in Live and a published pending revision in the workspace. An explicit status in the request body still wins, and outside a workspace the default stays FALSE. duplicate() uses the same decision and no longer calls autoSaveManager->delete() on the duplicate.

AutoSaveManager::entityIsConsideredNew() now always loads the Live version through WorkspaceAutoSave::loadLiveVersion() and returns FALSE if that Live entity is published, otherwise falls back to the default-title or duplicate-suffix check. In getEntityOperations() the branch that hid both publish and unpublish actions for drafts is removed, so a staged-published new page shows "Unpublish page". In the UI, PageStatusBadge shows "Draft" on isNew alone, and ChangeRow.tsx no longer checks isNew when deciding whether a page is unpublished.

For templates, ContentTemplate::createFromClientSide() restores the 1.x default 'status' => $data['status'] ?? FALSE. At publish, WorkspaceAutoSave::stageFallbackDrafts() calls ContentTemplate::autoSavePublish(), which sets status TRUE, so the template is enabled when its draft goes Live. A template created and never edited has no draft and stays disabled after publish. ADR 0022 is updated (content template created disabled; consequence 9 rewritten). A newly created page is now a pending change that appears in the review panel.

  • Committed: November 12, 2026 (22 days later)

item.title: #3592331: Update the preview in place on prop edits instead of reloading the iframe
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 7 files, +488/−31 · js +486/−31 · md +2
  • Diff: 4364e97
  • Discussion: #3592331 · 1 contributor · 4 comments

Summary

In the Canvas editor, editing a component's props no longer reloads the whole preview iframe when only one component instance changed. That instance's markup is replaced in the live preview, or, for an island whose only change is its props, the props attribute is updated so it re-renders without going blank. This removes the flicker and the refetching of all CSS and JavaScript on each edit. Any other difference, such as changed <head> assets or drupalSettings, still loads the whole document as before.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

A new inPlaceUpdate.ts provides findInPlaceUpdate(), which compares the previous and new preview HTML by common prefix and suffix. It finds the innermost canvas-start-…/canvas-end-… comment-marker pair enclosing the whole difference and returns null if the change lies outside any instance or nothing changed. applyInPlaceUpdate() locates the marker pair in the active iframe's document, and returns false if the markers are not siblings. Otherwise it detaches Drupal behaviors from the old elements with Drupal.detachBehaviors(element, null, 'unload'), unmounts removed canvas-island elements, inserts the new markup, and calls Drupal.attachBehaviors() on the markers' parent element. When the replaced content is a single canvas-island differing only in props, the attribute is set on the live element, and only if the decoded props differ.

IFrameSwapper tracks the HTML the active iframe shows and tries an in-place update first. It falls back to the hidden-iframe load and swap when none applies. Viewport gets an inPlaceUpdates counter so unsetUpdatingComponent still fires, since an in-place update changes neither loading flag. Because it works on HTML, it covers undo and redo with no API change.

Supporting changes: the canvasDisableLinks behavior now returns early when its context has no body, since behaviors can now run with an element context. The island custom element unmounts the previous render before re-rendering when ssr is set, and unmounts nested islands replaced by a render. The attributeChangedCallback workaround that deleted Preact's private VNode property is removed.

Upgrade

Custom Drupal behaviors that run in the Canvas preview may now receive an element as context rather than the document, as canvasDisableLinks was changed to handle. Guard any use of context.body and use once() so unchanged siblings are not initialized twice.

if (!context.body) {
  return;
}

  • Committed: November 12, 2026 (1 day later)

item.title: #3592337: Render headless previews on unpublished canonical entity pages
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 3 files, +195/−15 · php +180/−7 · md +15/−8
  • Diff: e69fecf
  • Discussion: #3592337 · 1 contributor · 4 comments

Summary

With Canvas headless, opening an unpublished node or Canvas page at its normal Drupal URL used to show an empty content area instead of the configured headless frontend, even for editors who could view the entity and had access canvas headless preview. The frontend is now embedded on unpublished canonical pages too, for users who already pass Drupal's access check and have that permission.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

EmbeddedPreviewSubscriber in canvas_headless previously skipped embedding when a non-preview canonical route's entity was an unpublished EntityPublishedInterface. That condition is removed. Route access has already decided whether the user may view the entity, and the embedded preview renders the same saved default revision with the user's own permissions. Authenticated-user and access canvas headless preview checks remain, so other visitors still get Drupal's normal rendering (or a 403 if access is denied).

The README section is renamed from 'Published route previews' to 'Canonical route previews' and notes two caveats: a canonical route renders the saved default revision without Canvas auto-saves, and the iframe replaces Drupal's rendered entity, including controls rendered as part of it such as Content Moderation's state form. Moderation state should be changed from the edit form. Kernel tests cover unpublished pages, nodes and translations, cache metadata, and HTTP-kernel access cases (200 embedded, 200 not embedded, 403).

item.title: #3592239: Workspaces PR 8: workspace management API and switcher UI
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Major unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 49 files, +3734/−64 · js +1967/−23 · php +1349/−11 · yml +318/−26 · css +76 · md +24/−4
  • Diff: c10aa3c
  • Discussion: #3592239 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

Canvas editors can now list, create, switch to and delete workspaces from a workspace switcher in the Canvas UI. When another workspace already holds pending changes to the entity being edited, the editor shows a lock notice with the owning workspace and, if the user may view it, a way to switch. Mutating Canvas API requests are also checked against the workspace the client says it is showing, so a second browser tab that switched workspaces cannot silently write into the wrong one. The CI rule that let Cypress and Playwright failures pass on the 1.x-workspaces branch is removed.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Permission change: Writing into a named (non-Main) workspace via a mutating canvas.api.* request now requires update access on that workspace.
  • New API: New hook_canvas_workspace_normalize_alter() and canvas.api.workspaces.* routes (list, create, delete, activate); optional X-Canvas-Workspace request header.

Technical details

ApiWorkspaceController (@internal) adds four routes: canvas.api.workspaces.list (GET, only top-level workspaces the user may view, plus activeWorkspaceId), create (POST with a label; the ID comes from the new WorkspaceMachineName service, validated with $workspace->validate(), 400 on failure), delete and activate. Delete uses the workspace access handler, so deleting Main is a 403; a workspace with child workspaces is a 409; deleting the active workspace first calls switchToLive(). Activation goes through WorkspaceManagerInterface::setActiveWorkspace(), so core negotiators and non-Canvas surfaces see the same workspace. WorkspaceNormalizer builds the Workspace payload (id, label, isDefault, isActive, pendingChangesCount, access.delete, access.publish) and invokes hook_canvas_workspace_normalize_alter().

WorkspaceRequestSubscriber runs on KernelEvents::REQUEST for POST/PATCH/PUT/DELETE on canvas.api.* routes, except canvas.api.workspaces.*, canvas.api.log_error and canvas.api.notifications.read. If X-Canvas-Workspace is present and differs from the session's staging workspace, it throws WorkspaceConflictException::noLongerExists() or ::notActive() (409). The header is optional, so clients such as the CLI that omit it bypass the check. When staging into a named workspace, the active workspace needs update access or the request gets a 403.

The layout response from ApiLayoutController gains lockedInWorkspace (id, label, canSwitch, updated, owner), built by buildWorkspaceLockInfo() from the new WorkspaceAutoSave::getOwningWorkspaceLockInfo(). It is only built for content entities; the owner is shown only if the current user has view label access. WorkspaceAutoSave::getOwningWorkspaceId() now also covers config entities: since core's tracker does not know config drafts, it looks for a fallback-store draft in another workspace, so a config draft is locked to one workspace at a time (the editor shows no notice for config, the second editor's write gets the 409). The editor boot settings gain workspaces.activeWorkspace via buildWorkspaceSettings(). ADR 0022 and openapi.yml document the error convention: 404 for an unknown ID in the URL, 409 with source.pointer: workspace for an unusable workspace, 409 EntityLockedInAnotherWorkspace for foreign-owned entities, 403 for refused access.

Upgrade

Implement the new alter hook to add keys to the workspace payload:

function hook_canvas_workspace_normalize_alter(array &$normalized, \Drupal\workspaces\WorkspaceInterface $workspace): void {
  $normalized['myModuleReviewed'] = (bool) $workspace->get('my_module_reviewed')->value;
}

Custom API clients that know their workspace may send X-Canvas-Workspace: <workspace id> on mutating requests to get a 409 instead of a write into the wrong workspace.

Contribution

  • Opened: October 21, 2026
  • Committed: November 11, 2026 (21 days later)

item.title: #3592316: A `type: array, items: {type: object …}` prop linked to a multi-valued entity field (`EntityFieldPropSource`) gets an object of lists, not a list of objects
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Critical bug report
  • Version: 1.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 8 files, +351/−15 · php +351/−15
  • Diff: acd9fe7
  • Discussion: #3592316 · 1 contributor · 4 comments

Summary

A type: array component prop with object items, linked to a multi-valued entity field in a content template, now receives a list of objects (one per field item). Before, it got a single object whose keys each held a list, so for example an image gallery with two images printed four empty <img> elements. No update path is needed, since only the expression is stored, not its evaluated value. Single-cardinality fields and expressions with an explicit delta evaluate as before.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: withDelta(int $delta): static added to EntityFieldBasedPropExpressionInterface and implemented by FieldPropExpression, FieldObjectPropsExpression and ReferenceFieldPropExpression.

Technical details

Evaluator::doEvaluate() evaluated each key of a FieldObjectPropsExpression over the whole field item list. Validation did not catch it, because core's ComponentMetadata added object to the type of every prop (per the issue; core 11.5 no longer does, see #3591948). StaticPropSource with FieldTypeObjectPropsExpression already evaluated once per field item.

Now, when the expression is a FieldObjectPropsExpression, the field cardinality is not 1 and getDelta() is NULL, doEvaluate() loops over the field items and re-evaluates $expr->withDelta($delta) for each. The results are merged into one EvaluationResult so cacheability and attachments of every object are kept, including objects that are then dropped. Empty objects (for instance when every object prop needs a referenced entity that was deleted) are filtered out and the list is reindexed with array_values(), so the type: array prop gets no gaps.

withDelta() is a new method on EntityFieldBasedPropExpressionInterface. FieldPropExpression sets the delta, FieldObjectPropsExpression sets it on itself and on every object prop expression, and ReferenceFieldPropExpression sets it only on the referencer, since the referenced expression targets another entity's field. Tests added: a multi-valued daterange case in EntityFieldPropSourceTest, rendering image-gallery with an unlimited image field in NodeTemplatesTest, broken-reference cases, and PropExpressionTest::testWithDelta().

Upgrade

Any custom class implementing EntityFieldBasedPropExpressionInterface must now implement public function withDelta(int $delta): static.

  • Committed: November 11, 2026 (1 day later)

item.title: #3592325: Mutations keep failing with a stale CSRF token when the 403 response has an HTML body
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 2 files, +55/−3 · js +55/−3
  • Diff: b09c8bc
  • Discussion: #3592325 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

In the Canvas editor, saving changes could keep failing after the session changed, for example after logging out and back in from another tab. This happened on routes that return an HTML 403 page, such as the headless frontend and component sync routes. The editor now recovers from these failures by fetching a fresh CSRF token and retrying. Users no longer have to reload the editor.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The editor reuses a cached session CSRF token (introduced in #3592277). When a mutation gets a 403, rawBaseQuery in ui/src/services/baseQuery.ts drops the cached token with forgetCsrfToken() and retries once. The retry condition checked result.error?.status === 403. With an HTML body, fetchBaseQuery cannot parse JSON and reports PARSING_ERROR as the error status, so the retry was skipped. The condition now checks result.meta?.response?.status === 403, which holds the HTTP status whatever the body is. A vitest test stubs fetch to return an HTML 403 for the stale token and checks that the request is resent with a new token.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: November 10, 2026
  • Committed: November 11, 2026

item.title: #3592238: Workspaces PR 7b: the workspace is the unit of publish (UI)
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Major unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 47 files, +1071/−1049 · js +998/−1039 · php +54/−1 · yml +19 · css +0/−9
  • Diff: e94a49f
  • Discussion: #3592238 · 1 contributor · 4 comments

Summary

In the 1.x-workspaces branch, the Canvas publish review panel now publishes the whole workspace at once. The per-change checkboxes, "Select all" and "Publish N selected" are gone, replaced by a single "Publish now" button and an "N unpublished changes" count. The side-by-side review button becomes "Review all changes", which walks every reviewable change. A conflicted change blocks publishing until it is resolved. Refusals that concern the workspace as a whole, such as core refusing to publish an item in an unpublished moderation state, now show in the error list under "Workspace".

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Permission change: Publishing now goes through core workspaces, so the e2e/test setups grant view any workspace, edit any workspace and create workspace alongside publish auto-saves.
  • New API: drupalSettings.canvas.workspaces.stagingWorkspaceId is now exposed to the UI, and a canvas_e2e_support.update_live test route (LiveEntityController::updateLive) saves the Live copy outside any workspace.

Technical details

ui/src/services/pendingChangesApi.ts: publishAllPendingChanges takes no argument. It POSTs to /canvas/api/v0/auto-saves/publish with { workspace, pendingChanges }. workspace comes from getStagingWorkspaceId(), which reads drupalSettings.canvas.workspaces.stagingWorkspaceId. The server now sets that value from workspaceAutoSave->getStagingWorkspaceId(), so a tab whose workspace was switched elsewhere cannot publish a different workspace. pendingChanges maps each auto-save key to its data_hash from the cached getAllPendingChanges result. Before building the body it waits for in-flight preview and layout auto-save mutations and refetches the list, so a publish right after an edit isn't refused as "edited after the review". On a 409 it restores the previous pending changes and sets the conflicts and errors. On success it clears the whole pending cache.

PublishReview loses its selection state, and onPublishClick is called without arguments. UnpublishedChanges passes all unpublished changes to the hook's cleanup. onReviewSelectedChanges is replaced by onReviewAllChanges, and conflicted pages and non-page changes are excluded from the walk. The review is still gated on isReviewUxEnabled(). A refused publish drops the snapshot, so discarding the refused changes afterwards doesn't flash "Published". ReviewErrors labels errors whose source.pointer is workspace as "Workspace". Errors tied to no entity (code 11 for a discarded key, validation violations, server errors, plain 403 strings) are counted in the header but not listed. Auto-save keys are now workspace-scoped (e.g. canvas_default:canvas_page:1:en). PageStatus therefore finds the homepage staged config update with findInChanges instead of an exact key lookup.

The Playwright specs were rewritten for this. canvas_e2e_support gets a LiveEntityController route that simulates external edits to Live, and a new article_moderation recipe fixture backs a spec checking that a draft moderation state refuses to publish. Two @todo Workspaces MR 8 and MR 9 markers remain for the workspace switcher, lock notice and Draft badge.

Upgrade

Tests or custom code that drove per-item publish must change. Replace the selection clicks (canvas-publish-review-select-all, Select change <title>, Publish N selected) with a click on the Publish now button. Test roles that publish need core workspace access, as in the updated setups:

'publish auto-saves',
'view any workspace',
'edit any workspace',
'create workspace',

Pending-change keys now carry the workspace prefix, for example canvas_default:canvas_page:${id}:en.

  • Committed: November 10, 2026 (19 days later)

item.title: #3592237: Workspaces PR 7a: the workspace is the unit of publish (back end)
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Major unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 24 files, +1616/−1489 · php +1578/−1471 · yml +38/−18
  • Diff: 45a7694
  • Discussion: #3592237 · 1 contributor · 2 comments

Summary

In the 1.x-workspaces branch, the Canvas publish endpoint now publishes the whole active workspace as one unit, through core's workspace publish, instead of publishing selected auto-save items one by one. The request must name the workspace and list the pending changes the editor reviewed. If the workspace is not the active one, or the pending list has changed since the review, the request is refused with a 409 and nothing is published. Any invalid item blocks the whole publish with a 422. Discarding a draft is now refused when the user cannot update the entity, or when another workspace has locked it.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Permission change: Publishing now also requires core's publish access to the active workspace, not only the Canvas publish permission. The publishChanges UI flag in drupalSettings follows the same rule. Discarding an auto-save now requires entity update access.
  • API change: POST /canvas/api/v0/auto-saves/publish now publishes the whole active workspace. The body must be {workspace, pendingChanges}, where pendingChanges maps auto-save key to data_hash. A body without them is a 400. Per-item selection and the old 409/424 codes for unexpected/unmatched items and global assets are gone. DELETE /canvas/api/v0/auto-saves/{entityTypeId}/{entityId} gains 403 and 409 responses.
  • New API: New \Drupal\canvas\Workspace\CanvasWorkspacePublisher service (marked @internal), new ErrorCodesEnum cases ActiveWorkspaceMismatch (10) and PendingChangesOutdated (11), and a BuildsAvatarUrlTrait.

Technical details

ApiAutoSaveController::post() is rewritten and the per-item machinery is removed: sibling-translation expansion, global asset dependency checks, applyAutoSaveTranslationSnapshots(), conflict-aware validation, the manual transaction, and AutoSaveManager::groupContentEntityAutoSaves(). post() returns a 400 if workspace or pendingChanges is missing. It throws WorkspaceConflictException::noLongerExists() or ::notActive() (codes 9 and 10) when the named workspace is gone or is not the active one. It checks core's publish access on the workspace and returns a 403 if denied. stalePendingChangesResponse() then compares the reviewed key => data_hash map with getPublishableAutoSaves(). It returns a 409 with one PendingChangesOutdated (code 11) error per added, edited or discarded key.

The actual publish goes through the new CanvasWorkspacePublisher::publish(). It wraps core's $workspace->publish() in a database transaction, covering the pre-publish subscribers that apply staged config as well as core's own revision promotion. It runs inside executeInWorkspace() and counts the auto-save rows for the success message. If the publish fails, it restores the previously active workspace, because core only switches back after the callback returns. If the published workspace was deleted and is still active in the session, it switches to Live. In the controller, WorkspacePublishValidationException maps to a 422 with one error per item, and any other WorkspacePublishException from core or a subscriber maps to a 409 with pointer workspace and no code. Other exceptions become a 500. An empty workspace returns 204 'No items to publish.'

ApiAutoSaveController::get() now adds the workspace cache context. delete() calls WorkspaceAutoSave::assertNotLockedInAnotherWorkspace() (409, with the owner in meta.workspace per openapi.yml) and checks entity update access after the 404 check. CanvasController computes publishChanges from the Canvas permission combined with core's publish access to the staging workspace, and adds that access result's cacheability to the response. buildAvatarUrl() moved into BuildsAvatarUrlTrait. ContentTemplate::autoSavePublish() is kept, because WorkspaceAutoSave::stageFallbackDrafts() still calls it. openapi.yml documents the new PublishAllRequest schema and the extra responses. Two @todo Workspaces MR 22 markers note that non-default-translation rows are still hidden from the pending list and the published count.

Upgrade

Clients of the publish endpoint must stop sending per-item selections. The body is now:

{
  "workspace": "spring_campaign",
  "pendingChanges": { "<auto-save key>": "<data_hash>" }
}

pendingChanges is the map returned by GET /canvas/api/v0/auto-saves/pending. Callers that relied on the old 409/424 item codes (UnexpectedItemInPublishRequest, UnmatchedItemInPublishRequest, GlobalAssetNotPublished) should handle the new codes 10 and 11 and the code-less 409 from a pre-publish gate. Users publishing need core's publish access to the workspace, which the tests grant through the edit any workspace permission.

Contribution

Timeline

item.title: #3592256: Add `dr canvas:audit:usage` command
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Major feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 14 files, +926/−175 · php +817/−171 · md +57/−4 · json +52
  • Diff: 23b82c3
  • Discussion: #3592256 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

Canvas now has a dr canvas:audit:usage command that lists where components are used. Give it a component source plugin ID (for example sdc), a component ID, or a component ID and version separated by @. It reports usages in content entity revisions, config entities (such as patterns) and auto-saves. This helps when you need to find where a known-broken component or version has been placed. Use --revisions=all|default|latest to narrow which content revisions are searched, and --format=table|json for human or machine output. The component audit page also now lists config entity usages only under the component version their tree actually uses. Before, it listed them without regard to version.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: ConfigAuditBase::getConfigEntityDependenciesUsingAuditTarget() and componentTreeUsesAuditTarget() accept $version_ids, getAutoSavesUsingAuditTarget() no longer throws for versions, and getComponentTreeConfigEntityTypeIds() is now public.
  • New API: New dr canvas:audit:usage command (requires Drupal >= 11.4 dr CLI) with a versioned --format=json report described by docs/audit-usage.schema.json.

Technical details

AuditUsageCommand (marked @internal) is a thin wrapper over the existing ComponentAudit service that powers the component audit page. It resolves the target to pairs of component and versions: a component source plugin ID expands to all components of that source, a bare component ID to all of its versions, and ID@version to one version. Unknown targets, unknown --format or --revisions values, and a missing target with --no-interaction exit with 2. When the target is omitted in interactive mode, it prompts for source, then component, then version.

The JSON report is an envelope with report_version (AuditUsageCommand::REPORT_VERSION, 1), target, revisions and usages. Each usage has component, version, kind (content, config or auto-save), entity_type, id, revision, default, latest and label. revision, default and latest are null for config and auto-save usages. Auto-save labels come from the auto-saved entity. The command first searches all requested versions at once, and only repeats the search per version when that finds something.

The audit layer needed version support to make this work. Config entity dependencies come from the config dependency graph, which does not track versions. So getConfigEntityDependenciesUsingAuditTarget() now takes $version_ids and inspects each dependent's component tree when versions are given. ComponentAudit::componentTreeUsesAuditTarget() checks getComponentVersion() on each item. ColorAudit throws a LogicException if versions are passed, since colors have no versions. The "not yet implemented" exception in getAutoSavesUsingAuditTarget() is removed. ComponentAuditController::createConfigTable() now passes [$component->getLoadedVersion()]. The diff also adds docs/cli.md, a contributor doc listing rules that every Canvas dr command must follow, and kernel tests.

Upgrade

Callers that previously relied on getConfigEntityDependenciesUsingAuditTarget($component, $type) ignoring versions are unaffected, because $version_ids defaults to []. To restrict to specific versions, pass them, for example getConfigEntityDependenciesUsingAuditTarget($component, $config_entity_type_id, [$version]). Subclasses of ConfigAuditBase must update their componentTreeUsesAuditTarget() signature to (ComponentTreeItemList $tree, ConfigEntityInterface $target, array $version_ids = []): bool.

item.title: #3592222: Canvas AI: Stopped turn's message is lost when tool calls are kept in history
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 4 files, +173/−32 · php +173/−32
  • Diff: bb653d3
  • Discussion: #3592222 · 1 contributor · 30 comments

Summary

When the Canvas AI option "Keep tool calls and results in the chat history" is on, a turn the user stopped no longer disappears from the agent's context. Before, typing "Continue" after pressing stop gave the agent only the earlier finished turn and "Continue", so it didn't know what to continue. Now the agent also receives the stopped turn's user message and the "You interrupted the agent. What would you like to change?" notice, as it already did with the option off.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

Each stored conversation checkpoint now records a message_count: the number of client transcript messages its turn was sent with, including its own user message. CanvasDevAiBuilder::storeConversationState() passes \count($prompt['messages']) to CanvasAiTempStore::setStoredConversationState(), which gained a required int $message_count parameter before $resumed_request_id. getStoredConversationState() now also returns message_count.

When a later turn resumes a checkpoint in prepareAgent(), the new private helper getMessagesAfterTurn() drops the first message_count transcript messages. It then skips the resumed turn's own narration and answer, which the checkpoint already holds, by starting at the first remaining user message. If no user message is left, nothing is appended. The remaining messages are appended to the restored history through setChatHistory().

The conversion was extracted from CanvasAiChatHelper::getFilteredChatHistory() into a new public CanvasAiChatHelper::toChatMessages(). It converts every message it is given and does not apply the maximum chat history messages limit. CanvasDevAiBuilder is marked @internal.

Upgrade

Checkpoints already in the tempstore have no message_count. getStoredConversationState() reads $record['message_count'] without a default, so a checkpoint written before this change may trigger an undefined array key warning when resumed. I did not verify how that case behaves.

item.title: #3592236: Workspaces PR 6: update path from 1.x
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Major unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 12 files, +897/−44 · php +896/−44 · yml +1
  • Diff: b554309

Summary

This is the 1.x update path for the Workspaces work, merged to the 1.x-workspaces branch. A 1.x site with unpublished Canvas drafts now keeps them when updating. A new post-update moves each draft into the Main workspace. It keeps the draft's content, its last editor and its last-edit time. Drafts whose entity or language no longer exists are dropped. Form validation error rows are re-keyed so they still match the migrated drafts. The update tests for the 1.x fixtures were adjusted to expect the drafts in workspace staging, and a new update test covers the migration.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Database update: New canvas_post_update_0031_migrate_auto_save_to_workspace() moves 1.x canvas.auto_save key-value drafts into the Main workspace and re-keys form violation rows with a main: prefix.

Technical details

canvas_post_update_0031_migrate_auto_save_to_workspace() is a batched post-update that handles 25 rows per pass. Each row goes through the new LegacyAutoSaveMigrator::migrate() (registered in canvas.services.yml), which resolves the target entity or translation and calls WorkspaceAutoSave::importLegacyArray() inside executeInWorkspaceUnchecked() for the Main workspace. Content entity rows are staged as workspace revisions inside a database transaction. Config entity rows are moved as they are into AutoSaveFallbackStore. If the entity already has staged content in Main (hasWorkspaceStaging()), the staged draft wins and the 1.x row is dropped. Malformed rows, rows for deleted entities, and rows for deleted languages are also dropped, along with their violation row.

A 1.x row holds one translation. The importer therefore overlays it onto a copy of the stored entity, or onto the revision already tracked in Main. That way sibling translations and the real default language survive publishing. The new legacyAttribution property lets stampAutoSaveWorkspaceRevisionMetadata() use the 1.x editor and edit time. If the 1.x editor user no longer exists, the current user is used. Under drush updb that is anonymous, and the code carries a @todo for it.

Once all rows are migrated, the post-update re-keys the form violation stores (FORM_VIOLATIONS_STORE and COMPONENT_INSTANCE_FORM_VIOLATIONS_STORE) under the AutoSaveWorkspace::ID . ':' prefix. It skips keys that already carry the prefix, so a re-run is safe. This happens in the post-update, not in canvas_update_11201(), because canvas_post_update_0010_migrate_auto_save() writes violation rows after every hook_update_N() has run. PageVariantMigration now migrates the page_region: rows itself, so its draft lookups find them. AutoSaveManager::overlaySnapshotOntoStored() became public, marked @internal for the importer.

The diff has no changes for the ServiceNotFoundException and Main-workspace lock failures that the issue lists as known bugs. It has no canvas_post_update_0032_workspace_permissions() and no canvas_update_11202() change either. I did not verify those items.

Upgrade

Run database updates as usual (drush updb). canvas_update_11201() enables Workspaces and creates Main, then canvas_post_update_0031_migrate_auto_save_to_workspace() migrates the 1.x drafts. Code that reads the canvas.auto_save key-value store directly will find it empty afterwards. Staged drafts are read through AutoSaveManager.

item.title: #3592265: Improve headless component sync compatibility with page templates
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 16 files, +522/−33 · js +339/−28 · php +163/−4 · md +10 · css +8 · mdx +2/−1
  • Diff: e8b34a9
  • Discussion: #3592265 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

In page templates used with a headless frontend, the Page content marker no longer vanishes in the editor preview in common cases. When a component sync removes the slot that holds Page content, the marker is now kept and placed right after its former container instead of being deleted with the slot. Headless previews no longer replace a slot that contains only Page content with an empty-slot placeholder. If the active frontend reports no editable content region, for example because it lacks the container component, the preview now shows a warning above the frame instead of silently leaving editors with nowhere to add components.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: ComponentTreeItemList::moveItemAfter() added; @drupal-canvas/headless-host geometry events gain an optional reset: true flag.

Technical details

In JsonSchemaPropsComponentInstanceUpdater, removed-slot handling now collects every descendant of the removed slots, walking up ancestors. Any item whose component ID is Marker::PAGE_CONTENT_COMPONENT_ID gets the container's parent_uuid and slot, and is moved after the container with the new ComponentTreeItemList::moveItemAfter(). The remaining collected subtrees are then filtered out. ComponentTreeConfigEntityBase::set() now drops explicit NULL parent_uuid and slot values from component_tree, because config represents them by omitting the keys. This matters when the marker moves to the root. The sync docs note the exception.

In the headless package, isCanvasComponentTreeSlotEmpty() now treats a string child as a default or example only when it contains no Canvas component comment markers, checked with parseCanvasCommentMarker() from @drupal-canvas/preview-geometry. Page content marker markup therefore counts as a real child and is rendered in the slot.

In @drupal-canvas/headless-host, the geometry event gets an optional reset?: true. The host sets it on activation, iframe reload, navigation and malformed snapshots, so a host reset can be told apart from a valid empty report from the frontend. In Canvas UI, useHeadlessDraftSession returns a new geometryReady value. A reset clears both geometry and height readiness. HeadlessPreview shows an amber Callout only when the preview is active, both height and geometry have been reported, and no region with id content exists. It keeps the previous iframe height while a reloaded document reports.

Upgrade

Consumers of @drupal-canvas/headless-host that handle geometry events can use the optional flag to tell a host reset from a real empty report:

| { type: 'geometry'; geometry: CanvasGeometry[]; reset?: true }

item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 26 files, +1039/−58 · php +698/−45 · js +333/−7 · md +7/−5 · yml +1/−1
  • Diff: 9a92022
  • Discussion: #3592235 · 1 contributor · 2 comments

Summary

On the 1.x-workspaces branch, the Canvas editor now works against the active workspace. Opening the editor with no active workspace switches to Main (when the user may view it). Drafts are read from the workspace, while page deletes, translation deletes and config translation override deletes act directly on Live. Deleting a page or translation that another workspace has staged changes for is refused with a 409 naming that workspace. Content create and status changes stay inside the workspace, and config entity writes through the Canvas config API still go to Live at once.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Permission change: Page delete access is now decided against Live (ApiContentControllers::deleteAccess()), so the delete link and route work while a workspace is active. Publish in tests needs edit any workspace.

Technical details

Core has no staged deletion and forbids deleting an entity Live has while a workspace is active. ApiContentControllers::delete() and ApiTranslationControllers::delete() therefore became instance methods that call WorkspaceAutoSave::assertNotLockedInAnotherWorkspace() and then wrap the delete in executeOutsideWorkspace() (from OptionalWorkspaceManagerTrait). The canvas.api.content.delete route swaps _entity_access for _custom_access: ApiContentControllers::deleteAccess, which checks delete access outside the workspace. The ::list() delete link uses the same check. The translation delete loads Live via loadLiveVersion(), removes the translation and saves outside the workspace. That save fires hook_entity_translation_delete(), which drops the translation from every workspace's staged copy. If the translation exists only in the active workspace's draft, it calls AutoSaveManager::deleteTranslation() instead. The two PHPStan ignores on $workspaceManager are removed now that it is read.

Route upcasting runs inside the workspace, so the upcast entity may be a staged revision. ApiLayoutController (layout GET and the label callback) and EntityFormController (AJAX POST rebuild) now call WorkspaceAutoSave::loadLiveVersion() when no auto-save data applies. In the layout GET, Live also becomes $original_entity, so isNew and hasUnsavedStatusChange are not computed against the staged revision. In the form rebuild, building from the staged revision would add extra rows to multi-value widgets. CanvasController::__invoke() loads the Main workspace (AutoSaveWorkspace::ID) and calls setActiveWorkspace() if none is active and the user has view access. The canvas_update_11201() guard still applies because $workspaceManager is nullable. ComponentInstanceForm now implements WorkspaceSafeFormInterface. Client side, brandKit.ts updateAutoSave now handles the returned autoSaves hash. Other UI service changes were not in the portion of the diff I read.

Several @todo Workspaces MR n: markers were added or retargeted. They cover the status default in ContentTemplate::createFromClientSide() (MR 9, templates are still created enabled), the lockedInWorkspace response key (MR 8), publish access (MR 7a) and whether Main stays active after leaving the editor (MR 16). The ADR text is updated: content create runs inside the workspace and templates are created enabled.

item.title: #3592234: Workspaces MR 4: component generation outside the workspace
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 11 files, +386/−60 · php +383/−56 · yml +1 · txt +1 · md +1/−4
  • Diff: e61b234
  • Discussion: #3592234 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

On the 1.x-workspaces branch, Canvas now generates Component config entities outside the active workspace. Component config generated from code, such as block components, is written to Live. It no longer piles up as pending changes in each workspace. Switching workspaces also no longer triggers a cascade of component regeneration inside the workspace. Code components are the exception. They are config entities edited in Canvas, so their generated Component follows them into the active workspace. Publishing a workspace draft of a code component's Component now requires update access to the code component, meaning the administer code components permission.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: ComponentSourceManager takes a new optional $workspaceManager constructor argument (@?workspaces.manager), and generated Components now save to Live unless their source sets discoveryReadsStagedConfig.
  • New API: New discoveryReadsStagedConfig property (default FALSE) on the ComponentSource plugin attribute, set TRUE on JsComponent.

Technical details

ComponentSourceManager::generateComponents() has a private $generating flag, set in a try/finally block. Saving Component config switches workspace context. That clears entity field definitions, which makes Layout Builder clear block plugin definitions. BlockManagerDecorator then calls back into generation, so nested calls return early. The finally block resets the flag after a failed pass.

The manager splits the source definitions in two. Sources whose definition has discoveryReadsStagedConfig TRUE are generated in the current workspace. All other sources are generated together in a single executeOutsideWorkspace() call, from the new OptionalWorkspaceManagerTrait. ComponentSourceManager gets an optional $workspaceManager constructor argument, wired as @?workspaces.manager in canvas.services.yml. The comment in the diff says it is NULL until a 1.x site has run canvas_update_11201().

The ComponentSource attribute gains a bool $discoveryReadsStagedConfig = FALSE property. JsComponent sets it to TRUE.

AutoSaveWorkspacePublishSubscriber no longer skips the access check for generated Components. The skip was previously inert and carried a @todo Workspaces MR 4. A new accessSubject() checks update access on the source JavaScriptComponent for JsComponent-sourced Components. It falls back to the Component itself if the code component is gone (ComponentNotFoundException).

The BlockComponent block settings subform class now also implements core's WorkspaceSafeFormInterface. Without it, core refuses to submit the form inside a workspace, so blockSubmit() was skipped. A kernel test showed this left multiplier at 0.

New and extended tests are ComponentSourceManagerWorkspaceTest, BlockComponentTest and WorkspaceAutoSaveStagingTest. The ADR text drops the sentence saying the block manager decorator regenerates only when the plugin ID set changed.

Upgrade

Custom ComponentSource plugins whose discovery reads workspace-staged config entities should opt in:

#[ComponentSource(
  // ...
  discoveryReadsStagedConfig: TRUE,
)]

Leaving the default (FALSE) generates the plugin's Component config against Live.

item.description:

Summary

In Canvas Brand Kit, choosing "Add color" from a color folder's menu could let the closing menu return focus to its trigger after the color popover had opened. If you typed into a field such as Alpha quickly, that late focus change blurred the field and could reset an invalid value, which re-enabled the Add button. The folder menu no longer takes focus back when it hands focus to the popover. Pressing Escape still returns focus to the menu trigger.

The Brand Kit colors section already used a suppressAutoFocusRef flag to stop the top-level dropdown's onCloseAutoFocus from restoring focus. The per-folder menus did not use it. The folder "Add color" menu item now sets suppressAutoFocusRef.current = true before opening the popover.

The handler is passed to the folder menus as a new optional onMenuCloseAutoFocus prop on FolderList. FolderList forwards it to SidebarFolder, which wires it to onCloseAutoFocus on both the dropdown and the context-menu UnifiedMenu.Content. Without the flag set, normal menu dismissal behaves as before.

A new Vitest spec for BrandKitColorsSection adds two tests. The first uses fake timers to enter an invalid Alpha (-0.5) before the menu's delayed focus return. It then asserts that the field keeps focus, the value stays, and the save button is disabled. The second asserts that Escape still returns focus to the menu trigger.
